sectorDetail.criteriaDesc: When determining the right raw material for this sector, we recommend clarifying the following points first.
sectorDetail.brandsTitle: Recommended LG Chem Product Families for This Sector
sectorDetail.linkNote: Click the product families below to view their grade lists and request TDS.
sectorDetail.supplyDesc: From our two warehouses on the European and Anatolian sides of Istanbul we offer same-day delivery within the city, and supply Europe through our Bucharest office.
sectorDetail.ctaTitle: Let's Determine the Right Raw Material for Your Sector
sectorDetail.ctaDesc: Tell us about your application and our technical team will identify suitable grades and provide TDS and sample support.
sectorDetail.s1intro1: The automotive sector is where demand for plastic raw materials is both highest and technically most demanding. Continuous high temperature under the hood, the surface quality expected in interior trim and the UV resistance required for exterior parts call for very different material properties.
sectorDetail.s1intro2: Weight reduction targets have accelerated the replacement of metal parts with engineering plastics. With the spread of electric vehicles, demand has risen markedly for flame retardant compounds with high electrical insulation for battery components, charging systems and high-voltage connectors.
sectorDetail.s2intro1: In the electrical and electronics sector, material selection usually starts with certification. The UL-94 flammability class, CTI value and RoHS compliance are preconditions for part approval.
sectorDetail.s2intro2: The trend towards miniaturisation requires high flow and flame retardancy at thin sections. Halogen-free flame retardant systems are increasingly requested due to environmental regulations and customer policies.
s2criteria: UL-94 class and the thickness it applies to
sectorDetail.s3intro1: Home appliances demand visible surface quality and long-term mechanical performance at the same time. On visible parts such as panels and covers, surface gloss and colour stability are decisive.
sectorDetail.s3intro2: For refrigerator interiors, washing machine components and parts around ovens, temperature resistance, detergent resistance and food contact suitability become critical. Using very different material families within the same product is therefore common.
sectorDetail.s4intro1: In construction and infrastructure the decisive criterion is longevity. Parts used on facades are exposed to UV, temperature swings and precipitation for years, and the material is expected to retain its mechanical properties throughout.
sectorDetail.s4intro2: Fire safety regulations are also decisive for building elements. In transparent roof and facade applications, impact strength and light transmission must be achieved together.
sectorDetail.s5intro1: In medical applications material selection must be considered together with the sterilisation method. Steam (autoclave), gamma and ethylene oxide sterilisation affect materials differently; some polymers can yellow or become brittle after gamma exposure.
sectorDetail.s5intro2: Transparency is critical in devices where fluid level must be visible. Biocompatibility and conformity with the relevant standards are preconditions for use in healthcare, so approval status must always be verified during grade selection.
sectorDetail.s6intro1: In furniture and household goods the material is usually visible and touched, so surface quality, colour consistency and tactile expectations matter as much as technical properties.
sectorDetail.s6intro2: For moving parts such as fittings, rails and hinges, friction resistance and fatigue strength come to the fore. Kitchenware in contact with food requires compliance approval.
sectorDetail.s7intro1: In defence and aerospace applications the expectation is to reduce weight without compromising performance. Metal replacement is the strongest motivation in this sector.
sectorDetail.s7intro2: Stability across a wide temperature range, fire safety and resistance to harsh environments are fundamental requirements. Depending on the application, electromagnetic shielding or static control may also be required.
s7criteria: Stability across a wide temperature range
sectorDetail.s8intro1: In agricultural applications the material stays outdoors for long periods. Continuous UV exposure, temperature swings and contact with agricultural chemicals fatigue the material, making UV stabilisation the most critical requirement.
sectorDetail.s8intro2: Irrigation systems additionally require continuous water contact and dimensional stability under pressure. Resistance to chemicals such as fertilisers and pesticides directly determines part life.
sectorDetail.s9intro1: In marine applications salt water is one of the most aggressive environments. Engineering plastics that replace metal parts because of corrosion offer a clear advantage in this sector.
sectorDetail.s9intro2: Continuous sun exposure brings UV resistance to the fore, while water contact highlights hydrolytic stability. In transport vehicles, fire safety and interior material regulations become decisive.
sectorDetail.s10intro1: In the toy sector safety comes before everything. The material is expected to comply with the relevant toy safety regulations, be free of heavy metals and meet contact conditions similar to food contact.
sectorDetail.s10intro2: Vivid colours, good surface quality and impact strength also matter; toys are dropped and stressed. The compatibility of colour pigments with the material is another point to watch.
s10criteria: Surface quality and absence of flash
sectorDetail.s11intro1: In lighting applications LED technology has changed material expectations. Light diffusion materials were developed to convert point-source light into homogeneous surface illumination.
sectorDetail.s11intro2: In energy applications, electrical insulation, flame retardancy and outdoor durability come to the fore. Photovoltaic junction boxes and energy storage systems have increased demand for halogen-free flame retardant and hydrolytically stable materials.
s11criteria: Balance of light transmission and diffusion

polymer.pp_homopolimer_intro1: Polypropylene homopolymer is the stiffest type in the PP family with the highest heat deflection temperature. Produced from a single monomer, it has a high degree of crystallinity, which brings strength and hardness advantages.
polymer.pp_homopolimer_intro2: Thanks to its low density, broad chemical resistance and favourable cost, it is used across a very wide range from packaging to industrial parts. However, its low-temperature impact strength is limited compared with copolymer types, which should be considered for cold environment applications.
polymer.pp_kopolimer_intro1: Block copolymer polypropylene is produced by adding an ethylene phase to the homopolymer structure. This addition markedly increases impact strength, particularly at low temperature.
polymer.pp_kopolimer_intro2: Toughness is gained at the expense of some stiffness. This balance is preferred for crates operating in cold environments, automotive parts and industrial components.
polymer.pp_random_intro1: In random copolymer polypropylene the ethylene units are distributed randomly along the chain. This structure lowers crystallinity and gives the material clarity and flexibility.
polymer.pp_random_intro2: It is preferred in packaging applications where transparency matters and in pipe systems requiring flexibility. It has a lower melting temperature than the homopolymer.
polymer.hdpe_intro1: Thanks to its linear chain structure, HDPE offers high crystallinity and consequently high stiffness and strength. It is the most durable member of the polyethylene family.
polymer.hdpe_intro2: Its excellent chemical resistance and low moisture permeability make it the standard material for liquid storage, pipe systems and packaging. Being easily recyclable is also an advantage for sustainability.
polymer.ldpe_intro1: LDPE has low crystallinity due to its branched chain structure, which makes it soft, flexible and easy to process.
polymer.ldpe_intro2: It is the base material for film applications; high elongation and good heat sealing are decisive in the packaging sector. It also offers good chemical resistance and electrical insulation performance.
polymer.gpps_intro1: GPPS is a rigid, dimensionally very stable amorphous thermoplastic with glass-like clarity. Its low shrinkage is an advantage for tight-tolerance parts.
polymer.gpps_intro2: Its easy processing and favourable cost make it widespread in consumer products. However, due to its brittle nature, HIPS or other impact-modified types should be considered for parts under impact loading.
polymer.hips_intro1: HIPS is produced by adding a rubber phase to polystyrene. This modification removes clarity but very markedly increases impact strength.
polymer.hips_intro2: Its thermoformability and good surface quality make it prominent in refrigerator liners and packaging applications. It is easy to paint and print on.
polymer.tpe_intro1: TPEs are a material class that combines the flexibility of rubber with the processability of thermoplastics. As they require no vulcanisation, they can be injection moulded in series production and recycled.
polymer.tpe_intro2: Being available at different hardness levels lets a single material family serve very different applications. Through two-component moulding they can be bonded to rigid plastics to create soft-touch grip surfaces.
polymer.tpu_intro1: TPU is one of the strongest elastomers in terms of abrasion resistance and mechanical strength. It shows very good tear and scratch resistance while retaining high elasticity.
polymer.tpu_intro2: Thanks to its oil and fuel resistance it is preferred in industrial and automotive applications. With hard and soft types it offers a wide hardness range.
polymer.eva_intro1: EVA is a copolymer of ethylene and vinyl acetate. As the vinyl acetate content rises the material becomes softer, clearer and more adhesive.
polymer.eva_intro2: Its flexibility and impact damping in foam applications make it widespread in footwear and sports equipment. It is also the base material for solar panel encapsulation films.
polymer.abs_intro1: ABS is an amorphous engineering plastic formed from three monomers: acrylonitrile provides chemical resistance, butadiene toughness, and styrene processability and surface quality.
polymer.abs_intro2: Being platable and paintable is a major advantage for visible surface parts. Its low shrinkage and dimensional stability make it preferred for tight-tolerance parts. Flame retardant and glass fibre reinforced compound types are available.
polymer.polikarbonat_intro1: Polycarbonate has one of the highest impact strengths among engineering plastics and can combine this with glass-like optical clarity. It retains its mechanical properties across a wide temperature range.
polymer.polikarbonat_intro2: With flame retardant, UV stable, glass fibre reinforced and light-diffusing special types, it is used from automotive lighting to medical devices. As it is hygroscopic, drying before processing is critical.
polymer.pmma_intro1: PMMA has the highest optical clarity among plastics, with light transmission even higher than glass. Thanks to its inherent UV resistance it can remain outdoors for long periods without yellowing.
polymer.pmma_intro2: Its surface hardness and scratch resistance are better than polycarbonate; however, its impact strength is markedly lower. It is therefore preferred where visual quality is the priority and impact loading is limited.
polymer.pbt_intro1: PBT is a semi-crystalline polyester that stands out among engineering plastics for its electrical insulation performance. Its fast crystallisation allows moulding at short cycle times.
polymer.pbt_intro2: Much lower moisture uptake than polyamides and superior dimensional stability are the main reasons it is preferred for precision electrical parts. Flame retardant and glass fibre reinforced types are widespread.
polymer.san_intro1: SAN is a copolymer of styrene and acrylonitrile. The acrylonitrile content provides markedly better chemical resistance and thermal performance than polystyrene while preserving clarity.
polymer.san_intro2: With high stiffness and dimensional stability it is used where transparent yet durable parts are required. It is harder but more brittle than ABS.
polymer.pc_abs_intro1: PC/ABS alloys bring together the impact strength and thermal performance of polycarbonate with the processability and cost advantage of ABS. The balance can be tuned to the application by changing the alloy ratio.
polymer.pc_abs_intro2: They are very common in automotive interior trim and electronic housings. They mould more easily than neat polycarbonate and offer markedly higher thermal and mechanical performance than neat ABS.
polymer.ppo_ppe_intro1: Modified PPO/PPE alloys are among the lowest density groups within engineering plastics and absorb virtually no moisture. This translates into outstanding dimensional stability.
polymer.ppo_ppe_intro2: Thanks to halogen-free flame retardant formulations and hydrolytic stability, they are preferred in photovoltaic junction boxes, battery components and parts in contact with hot water.
polymer.pa6_pa66_intro1: Polyamides are the most widely used family of engineering plastics, offering high mechanical strength, wear resistance and thermal performance. PA66 has a higher melting temperature than PA6.
polymer.pa6_pa66_intro2: Glass fibre reinforcement markedly raises stiffness and heat deflection temperature. Polyamides are highly hygroscopic; since moisture uptake affects dimensions and mechanical properties, drying and storage conditions must be followed strictly.

nobreak.catDesc: Ultra high impact PP block copolymer grades for parts that must not break. We supply products from SK Geo Centric, Hanwha TotalEnergies and Borealis / Borouge from stock and to order.
nobreak.intro1: Known in the industry as "no break", these are ultra high toughness PP types that offer markedly higher impact strength than standard block copolymer polypropylene. By optimising the ratio and distribution of the rubber phase, the part is designed to deform rather than break under impact.
nobreak.intro2: These grades are used particularly where breakage is unacceptable — crates, heavy duty pails, juvenile care products, appliance components and automotive parts. In applications operating at low temperature, cold impact strength becomes the decisive criterion.
nobreak.intro3: Since toughness is gained at the expense of some stiffness, the right grade must be selected according to the impact-versus-stiffness balance of the application. The flow (MFI) choice relates directly to part wall thickness and mould filling distance.
nobreak.gradesTitle: No Break PP Grades We Supply
nobreak.gradesDesc: You can request a technical data sheet (TDS), samples and pricing for each grade.
nobreak.selectionTitle: What to Consider When Selecting a Grade
nobreak.selectionDesc: Clarifying the points below is enough to determine the right no break grade.
nobreak.sel1: At what temperature will the part take impact? (room temperature or cold)
nobreak.sel2: What is the wall thickness and mould filling distance? (flow selection)
nobreak.sel3: Is stiffness or toughness the priority?
nobreak.sel4: Is food or child contact approval required?
nobreak.sel5: Will it be compounded or moulded directly?
nobreak.sel6: Will colouring or masterbatch be used?

nobreak.faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions About No Break PP
nobreak.faqQ1: What is no break PP and how does it differ from standard PPC?
nobreak.faqA1: No break PP is the common industry name for ultra high toughness types that offer much higher impact strength than standard block copolymer polypropylene (PPC). By optimising the ratio and distribution of the rubber phase, the part deforms rather than breaks under impact. In return, some stiffness is given up.
nobreak.faqQ2: Which no break PP grades do you supply?
nobreak.faqA2: We supply SK Geo Centric YUPLENE BH3500 and BH3820, Hanwha TotalEnergies BI6300 and BI7300, and Borealis / Borouge BD265MO. You can also write to us for a grade not listed — we will check availability and get back to you.
nobreak.faqQ3: How can I obtain the TDS for these grades?
nobreak.faqA3: Click "Access TDS" on the page of the grade you are interested in and leave your email and phone number. Your request reaches our sales team and the manufacturer's official technical data sheet is shared by email as soon as possible.
nobreak.faqA4: Yes. You can request samples for trial production and commissioning. Simply use the "Request Sample" button on the grade pages and leave your contact details.
nobreak.ctaDesc: Contact our sales team for quantity, lead time and pricing.
nobreak.tdsNote: No numerical technical values are published on this page. Values such as melt flow index, Izod impact strength, density and processing conditions appear in the manufacturer's official TDS — we do not share estimated values.
nobreak.sk_bh3500_desc: An ultra high impact polypropylene block copolymer from SK Geo Centric's YUPLENE series. Alongside impact strength it stands out for its balance of stiffness, flow and heat resistance.
nobreak.sk_bh3820_desc: The ultra high impact, high flow block copolymer type in SK Geo Centric's YUPLENE series. Developed for thin wall and very high speed injection moulding applications.
nobreak.hanwha_total_bi6300_desc: A high impact polypropylene block copolymer developed by Hanwha TotalEnergies for injection applications. Its high isotactic PP base and optimised rubber phase deliver a balance of stiffness and toughness.
nobreak.hanwha_total_bi7300_desc: Hanwha TotalEnergies' super impact resistance injection grade block PP. With high flowability and processability it is developed for automotive composite base, household goods parts and industrial material applications.
nobreak.borealis_bd265mo_desc: A very high impact heterophasic copolymer produced with Borstar Nucleation Technology (BNT). It shows excellent impact strength even at low temperatures and is approved for food and child contact.
